methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native demonstrate grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge distribution outside metro hubs, directly addressing the technology gap through distributed learning rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for community-wide AI education and innovation, suggesting potential for deep capability building distributed beyond just university researchers into Richmond's broader civic fabric.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly identifies AI data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide, signaling that current infrastructure investments concentrate economic benefits in NoVA while dispersing environmental costs without distributing capability or opportunity.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National
signals.signal_reading: Children's National and Virginia Tech collaboration creates deep AI capability in pediatric healthcare, but partnership between DC-adjacent institution and Blacksburg hub reinforces concentration in existing research centers rather than distributing expertise regionally.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's AI help assistant represents shallow platform-delivered adoption—workers gain efficiency through interfaces without building underlying AI capability, creating productivity gains without deep technical fluency transfer to the regional workforce.
